finding.claim: The /users route has no authentication or authorization check. The org filter is taken straight from the query string, so any unauthenticated caller can list the id and name of every user in any organization (IDOR / broken access control). This assumes no auth or tenant-scoping middleware exists elsewhere. db.js is the only source file in the repo, and no middleware is registered on `app`.
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET /users?org=<any org> on port 3002; req.query.org is fully attacker-controlled
finding.sink: req.pg.query("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1", [req.query.org]) returning rows to the caller via res.json

trace.note: Express app created; no app.use() for auth, session or tenant middleware is registered
GET /users handler has no per-route auth guard
Attacker-supplied org is used as the tenant filter with no comparison to the caller's own org
Matching rows are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: The SQL is parameterized ($1), so there is no SQL injection. No authentication, session, or org-ownership check is present in this file. I found no middleware, and req.pg is not defined anywhere in the repo, so any guard would have to live outside this codebase. Checked and found safe: /file (path.resolve plus a startsWith(ROOT + path.sep) check blocks traversal; sendFile denies dotfiles by default) and /count (execFile with fixed arguments, so no command injection).

verdict.guard_found: none (only parameterized SQL at db.js:9, which prevents injection but not access control)
verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no app.use() or per-route auth, and passes attacker-controlled req.query.org to the query at db.js:9 and returns the rows at db.js:10, so any anonymous caller can list users of any org; req.pg is never set here, so any guard would have to be outside this repo, which is a residual caveat.
